We have a task: determine SMILES string of an unknown organic compound sample, using minimal resources. We have only one data: proton NMR spectra returned: "Deltas 7.51 (dddd, J = 8.4, 7.4, 1.4, 0.4 Hz, 10H)." That's a single signal at 7.51 ppm, integration 10H, multiplicity dddd (doublet of doublet of doublet of doublet). That suggests a symmetrical aromatic system with 10 aromatic protons, likely biphenyl (C12H10) which has 10 aromatic protons, but biphenyl has two sets of aromatic protons maybe overlapping? Actually biphenyl (C12H10) has 10 aromatic protons, but due to symmetry, there are two sets: ortho protons (2H) around 7.5, meta (2H) around 7.3, para (2H) around 7.4? Not sure. But a single signal integrating to 10H suggests a highly symmetric aromatic, maybe phenylbenzene (biphenyl) where all protons are equivalent? In biphenyl, due to rotation, the rings are not coplanar, but the protons are not all equivalent; there are different chemical shifts. However in NMR, biphenyl shows multiple signals. So maybe the sample is a simple aromatic like naphthalene (C10H8) has 8 protons, not 10. Phenylbenzene? Actually biphenyl has 10 protons, but they are not all equivalent; but maybe the instrument resolution merges them into one broad multiplet? The multiplicity dddd suggests coupling to four neighboring protons, typical for a para-disubstituted benzene (AA'BB' pattern) gives doublet of doublet? But integration 10H suggests two phenyl rings each with 5H (monosubstituted phenyl). So maybe the compound is diphenyl ether? That also has 10 aromatic protons. But the signal at 7.51 dddd suggests each phenyl ring is monosubstituted, giving typical pattern of a monosubstituted phenyl: multiplet around 7.2-7.4 integrating to 5H. Two such rings give 10H overlapping. So the SMILES could be "c1ccccc1c2ccccc2" (biphenyl). That matches our earlier guess.

We can validate by searching for SMILES "c1ccccc1c2ccccc2" (biphenyl). Use search_by_smiles but that tool is broken. Could use carbon_nmr_shifts? Not needed. Could retrieve formula from SMILES to confirm? Use get_formula_from_smiles.
